scope: Seed traceability covering documented application modules; refine to feature/criterion IDs before implementation. No application is implemented.

requirements.title: Shared customer identity
requirements.description: One person identity spans brands; household contacts do not force a merge.
requirements.securityPrivacy: Apply current grants/scope, minimise sensitive data and preserve trustworthy history.
acceptanceCriteria: positive: Given two records sharing one canonical contact, When an agent selects the explicitly disambiguated person, Then the case attaches to that exact customer ID and both histories stay separate.
negative: Given a household contact shared by two persons, When intake resolves the contact, Then neither person is auto-merged and the agent must choose.
prohibited: Given any case or correction flow, When a duplicate or merge is attempted, Then creating a duplicate customer master or silently merging identities is prohibited.
boundary: Given an ambiguous person with exactly two candidate records, When the agent picks one, Then the chosen ID is recorded and the rejected candidate remains untouched.
failure: Given a concurrent competing correction to the same customer, When both commits race, Then one wins deterministically by revision and the loser is rejected without data loss.
requirements.verificationMethod: API identity/alias/shared-contact and concurrent correction cases

requirements.title: Controlled intake
requirements.description: Lookup precedes issue form; active dependent choices and original wording are retained.
requirements.securityPrivacy: Apply current grants/scope, minimise sensitive data and preserve trustworthy history.
acceptanceCriteria: positive: Given an existing customer and active catalogue choices, When the agent completes intake, Then the original wording and dependent choices are retained on the new case.
negative: Given a person switch mid-form, When the draft depended on the previous person, Then that draft is cleared while same-person history is kept.
prohibited: Given an unknown label, When it is entered during intake, Then it cannot create a master record from free text.
boundary: Given the last active option in a dependent list, When selected, Then intake succeeds; any inactive option is rejected.
failure: Given a malformed or oversized intake request, When submitted, Then it is rejected at the boundary and never reaches business logic.

requirements.title: Manager classification
requirements.description: Unknown category creates scoped eligible manager obligation that generic completion cannot bypass.
requirements.securityPrivacy: Apply current grants/scope, minimise sensitive data and preserve trustworthy history.
acceptanceCriteria: positive: Given an unknown-category case, When an eligible manager classifies it, Then the original message is preserved and only the applicable classification task completes.
negative: Given a case with no eligible manager, When create is attempted, Then it is blocked.
prohibited: Given a generic completion action, When it is used to complete the task, Then it cannot bypass the classification obligation.
boundary: Given a manager with the right role but wrong market, When classification is attempted, Then it is denied at the eligibility boundary.
failure: Given a classification task racing case closure, When both commit, Then closure waits or fails and the obligation cannot be hidden.

requirements.title: Claims and collaboration
requirements.description: Assignment, current worker and task owner remain separate with explicit takeover and stale-version protection.
requirements.securityPrivacy: Apply current grants/scope, minimise sensitive data and preserve trustworthy history.
acceptanceCriteria: positive: Given an unassigned case, When a worker claims it, Then assignment, current worker and task owner are stored as separate fields.
negative: Given a live other-worker edit, When a stale save arrives, Then it is refused without losing the local draft.
prohibited: Given any takeover, When a worker takes over, Then silent reassignment without an explicit takeover action is prohibited.
boundary: Given the configured working lease (D-07, proposed test value 120s), When it has just expired, Then takeover becomes possible; one second before, it is refused.
failure: Given a worker crash mid-edit, When the lease expires, Then another worker can take over and miss/ownership history is preserved.
requirements.verificationMethod: Concurrent API and browser claim/takeover cases

requirements.title: Shared discovery search
requirements.description: Authorised whitelisted linked fields support broad discovery distinct from exact identity lookup.
requirements.businessJustification: Find cases without leaking hidden fields.
requirements.securityPrivacy: Apply current grants/scope, minimise sensitive data and preserve trustworthy history.
acceptanceCriteria: positive: Given a formatted phone query, When search runs, Then it matches the real phone fields through the authorised projection.
negative: Given a field outside the whitelist, When included in the query, Then it is denied and never returned.
prohibited: Given a partial search result, When it is used to pick a customer, Then it must never auto-select an identity or grant write/export rights.
boundary: Given a query matching zero authorised fields, When submitted, Then an empty result is returned without information leakage.
failure: Given an authorisation-service failure during search, When queried, Then the request fails closed with no results.

requirements.title: Revisioned service decisions
requirements.description: Only exact current final approved revision enables consequential execution.
requirements.securityPrivacy: Apply current grants/scope, minimise sensitive data and preserve trustworthy history.
acceptanceCriteria: positive: Given a final approved revision, When the exact current revision executes, Then the consequential action commits against that revision.
negative: Given a need-info state, When a final decision is attempted, Then it is refused until scope and revision are final.
prohibited: Given any service decision, When a decision is executed, Then executing twice or against a superseded revision is prohibited.
boundary: Given shipped/received/waiver constraints on a revision, When an edit is attempted, Then it is refused once the constraint applies.
failure: Given a concurrent dispatch race, When decision and dispatch commit together, Then exactly one ordering wins and the other is safely rejected.

requirements.title: Allowed manager self-approval
requirements.description: Eligible managers may approve their own/materially edited request under ordinary scope rules.
requirements.securityPrivacy: Apply current grants/scope, minimise sensitive data and preserve trustworthy history.
acceptanceCriteria: positive: Given an eligible manager’s own materially edited request, When they approve it, Then the approval succeeds with identity, scope and audit recorded.
negative: Given a custom title or wrong market, When self-approval is attempted, Then it fails under ordinary scope rules.
prohibited: Given any non-manager or automated agent, When the approval is submitted, Then approving as a manager is prohibited.
boundary: Given a manager who is not eligible for the scope, When approval is attempted, Then it is denied exactly at the eligibility boundary.
failure: Given an audit-write failure, When self-approval commits, Then the approval is not recorded as valid.
requirements.verificationMethod: Policy/API positive self-approval and prohibited authority cases

requirements.title: Replacement paths
requirements.description: Return-first, advance and no-return paths retain independent exact inbound/outbound obligations.
requirements.securityPrivacy: Apply current grants/scope, minimise sensitive data and preserve trustworthy history.
acceptanceCriteria: positive: Given an approved return-first path, When the inbound receipt is due or damaged, Then dispatch is blocked until it is resolved.
negative: Given an advance replacement path, When the replacement ships, Then the inbound obligation remains open.
prohibited: Given a no-return path, When dispatch is requested, Then dispatch requires explicit approved assent; it is never inferred.
boundary: Given the exact approved scope, When quantity or address deviates by any amount, Then dispatch is refused.
failure: Given closure racing a new obligation, When both commit, Then closure fails and the obligation stands.

requirements.title: Cancellation fallback
requirements.description: External cancellation result is separate from approval and failed dispatch needs valid same-ticket full-coverage Return.
requirements.securityPrivacy: Apply current grants/scope, minimise sensitive data and preserve trustworthy history.
acceptanceCriteria: positive: Given an external cancellation result, When recorded on the same ticket, Then it is stored separately from the original approval.
negative: Given an already dispatched order, When cancellation is confirmed, Then it is refused.
prohibited: Given an incomplete or wrong fallback, When it is recorded, Then it cannot settle the original obligation.
boundary: Given a failed dispatch needing fallback, When a full-coverage Return is created on the same ticket, Then the original obligation stays open until the Return completes.
failure: Given an uncertain provider side effect, When the result is unknown, Then no settlement is recorded and the case stays pending.

requirements.title: Physical receipts and inspection
requirements.description: Cumulative entry appends immutable physical events and current-scope inspection.
requirements.securityPrivacy: Apply current grants/scope, minimise sensitive data and preserve trustworthy history.
acceptanceCriteria: positive: Given a cumulative entry, When quantities are recorded, Then immutable physical events append with current-scope inspection.
negative: Given a carrier status or matching change, When it occurs, Then no received quantity changes.
prohibited: Given under, over, fractional or future-dated input, When it is submitted, Then it fails atomically with no partial receipt.
boundary: Given the exact approved quantity, When the last unit is received, Then the receipt completes; one further unit is refused.
failure: Given a receipt racing a pending waiver, When both commit, Then the receipt supersedes the stale waiver without rewriting the approval.

requirements.title: Collection waiver
requirements.description: Manager waives only outstanding quantities on exact snapshot; receipt stays separate.
requirements.securityPrivacy: Apply current grants/scope, minimise sensitive data and preserve trustworthy history.
acceptanceCriteria: positive: Given an exact snapshot with outstanding quantities, When a manager waives, Then only the outstanding quantities are waived and the receipt stays separate.
negative: Given a late receipt after waiver, When it arrives, Then the effective waiver reduces without rewriting the original approval.
prohibited: Given any user below manager authority, When a waiver is requested, Then waiving is prohibited.
boundary: Given zero outstanding quantities, When waiver is attempted, Then it is refused because there is nothing to waive.
failure: Given a receipt/waiver race in either order, When both commit, Then the outcome is deterministic and audited, never double-counted.
requirements.verificationMethod: Both-order receipt/waiver races and late-arrival UAT

requirements.title: Unmatched parcels
requirements.description: Verified parcel identity match finishes identity task without creating receipt/payment.
requirements.securityPrivacy: Apply current grants/scope, minimise sensitive data and preserve trustworthy history.
acceptanceCriteria: positive: Given a verified parcel identity match, When confirmed, Then the identity task finishes without creating a receipt or payment.
negative: Given a wrong-warehouse parcel, When matching is attempted, Then it fails safely and the parcel stays unmatched.
prohibited: Given any match, When a match is confirmed, Then inventing customer fulfilment from an unverified parcel is prohibited.
boundary: Given concurrent matches on the same parcel, When both commit, Then exactly one succeeds.
failure: Given a matching-service failure, When attempted, Then the badge reflects the current unmatched state and no partial link persists.

requirements.title: Refund authority
requirements.description: Exact verified order/currency/scope/amount manager authority precedes external-result entry.
requirements.securityPrivacy: Apply current grants/scope, minimise sensitive data and preserve trustworthy history.
acceptanceCriteria: positive: Given exact verified order, currency, scope and amount, When a manager grants authority, Then external-result entry is enabled against that authority.
negative: Given a rejected amendment, When reverted, Then the prior approved amount and attempts are restored.
prohibited: Given any duplicate live authority, When a second authority is requested, Then a second concurrent authority for the same obligation is blocked.
boundary: Given the exact eligible amount, When one unit more is requested, Then it is refused.
failure: Given a stale concurrent refund attempt, When it races the current authority, Then it is rejected without effect.

requirements.title: Financial attempts
requirements.description: Pending/unknown reserves authority; success pays; failure releases; final outcomes immutable.
requirements.securityPrivacy: Apply current grants/scope, minimise sensitive data and preserve trustworthy history.
acceptanceCriteria: positive: Given a pending or unknown result, When recorded, Then the authority stays reserved until a final outcome.
negative: Given a failed attempt, When recorded, Then the reservation is released.
prohibited: Given paid plus reserved totals, When a new attempt is added, Then they must never exceed the granted authority.
boundary: Given blank proof or a duplicate provider reference, When submitted, Then it fails; a retry uses a distinct reference.
failure: Given a provider timeout with an uncertain side effect, When reconciled later, Then no duplicate payment is created.
requirements.verificationMethod: Concurrent real-DB reservation and reconciliation cases

requirements.title: Disputes
requirements.description: Provider deadline/evidence/state is independent of internal follow-up and checked at closure.
requirements.securityPrivacy: Apply current grants/scope, minimise sensitive data and preserve trustworthy history.
acceptanceCriteria: positive: Given a provider deadline, evidence and state, When the case closes, Then closure checks the independent dispute domain.
negative: Given a draft dispute, When viewed, Then it is not presented as submitted.
prohibited: Given a final provider result, When a state change is requested, Then downgrading it is prohibited.
boundary: Given an unresolved dispute with a missing follow-up task, When closure is attempted, Then closure is still blocked.
failure: Given a provider integration timeout, When the state is unknown, Then closure is refused and the case stays open.

requirements.title: All-obligation closure
requirements.description: Resolve/Close recheck every current domain fact and open task transactionally; reopen preserves history.
requirements.securityPrivacy: Apply current grants/scope, minimise sensitive data and preserve trustworthy history.
acceptanceCriteria: positive: Given Resolved state plus customer assent, When Close executes, Then every current domain fact and open task is rechecked in one transaction.
negative: Given any open obligation, When Close executes, Then it fails and nothing changes.
prohibited: Given any closure path, When closure is attempted, Then bypassing a domain gate is prohibited.
boundary: Given the last open obligation, When it completes and Close executes immediately, Then closure succeeds.
failure: Given a new obligation racing closure, When both commit, Then the gate holds and an unsupported final state is impossible.
requirements.verificationMethod: Real-DB closure race and per-gate UAT

requirements.title: Durable follow-ups
requirements.description: Independent eligible source/stage tasks preserve original deadline/first miss owner and actual/recorded completion.
requirements.securityPrivacy: Apply current grants/scope, minimise sensitive data and preserve trustworthy history.
acceptanceCriteria: positive: Given an eligible source/stage task, When created, Then the original deadline and first-miss owner are preserved.
negative: Given a snooze, reassign or reschedule, When applied, Then the recorded miss is not erased.
prohibited: Given any completion, When completion is recorded, Then affecting a task outside the applicable source is prohibited.
boundary: Given the exact completion for one applicable source, When recorded, Then only that source is affected.
failure: Given clock or timezone ambiguity, When due-work is computed, Then the canonical timezone applies and backdating needs explicit authority.

requirements.title: Reliable background work
requirements.description: Scheduler/outbox/inbox operate with browser closed and duplicate-safe recovery.
requirements.securityPrivacy: Apply current grants/scope, minimise sensitive data and preserve trustworthy history.
acceptanceCriteria: positive: Given committed work with the browser closed, When the scheduler runs, Then the next work happens exactly once.
negative: Given a lost response after commit, When retried, Then no second effect is accepted.
prohibited: Given any replay, When an event is replayed, Then duplicate business effects are prohibited.
boundary: Given a crash exactly at the commit boundary, When recovery runs, Then the outcome is one accepted effect with retained miss evidence.
failure: Given an outbox, inbox or queue crash or duplicate event, When recovered, Then idempotency dedupes and nothing is lost.
requirements.verificationMethod: Worker crash boundaries and DLQ replay

requirements.title: Governed analytics
requirements.description: Defined created-cohort and first-miss metrics use canonical timezone/filters and explicit unknown coverage.
requirements.securityPrivacy: Apply current grants/scope, minimise sensitive data and preserve trustworthy history.
acceptanceCriteria: positive: Given defined created-cohort and first-miss metrics, When computed, Then canonical timezone/filters apply and drilldowns reconcile to rows.
negative: Given an unavailable denominator, When computed, Then it is marked unknown, not zero.
prohibited: Given any metric, When it is published or compared, Then silently changing its definition is prohibited.
boundary: Given the half-open final-day boundary, When evaluated, Then the final day is included exactly once.
failure: Given clock or timezone skew, When metrics run, Then the canonical timezone governs and the anomaly is detectable.

requirements.title: Eight complete exports
requirements.description: Stable versioned schemas retain full filtered evidence and safe CSV encoding with download reauthorisation.
requirements.securityPrivacy: Apply current grants/scope, minimise sensitive data and preserve trustworthy history.
acceptanceCriteria: positive: Given the full filtered cohort, When one of the eight exports runs, Then the parsed file matches the cohort exactly with safe CSV encoding.
negative: Given revoked access, When a download link is used, Then it is refused.
prohibited: Given any export, When an export is generated, Then exporting hidden or unauthorised fields is prohibited.
boundary: Given Unicode or nested-history edge cases, When encoded, Then parsing round-trips without corruption or formula injection.
failure: Given a partially failed export job, When resumed, Then either the full consistent file or no file is delivered.

requirements.title: Legacy migration
requirements.description: Real preview/review/publish uses source IDs, stale/conflict handling and known-vs-unknown history.
requirements.securityPrivacy: Apply current grants/scope, minimise sensitive data and preserve trustworthy history.
acceptanceCriteria: positive: Given a real preview/review/publish cycle, When published, Then source IDs, known-versus-unknown history and reconciled balances are preserved.
negative: Given newer manual data, When a replay conflicts, Then it is held as a conflict, not overwritten.
prohibited: Given ambiguous people, When records are matched during import, Then merging them during import is prohibited.
boundary: Given an unchanged re-import, When replayed, Then it no-ops.
failure: Given a stale or replayed import or schema mismatch, When detected, Then publishing halts and prior state is intact.

requirements.title: User/role access lifecycle
requirements.description: Current union grants and scope govern commands; access removal cannot strand work/final admin.
requirements.securityPrivacy: Apply current grants/scope, minimise sensitive data and preserve trustworthy history.
acceptanceCriteria: positive: Given current union grants and scope, When a command executes, Then it is authorised against the live state.
negative: Given a removed grant, When the same still-valid token is presented, Then the request is denied because access is re-checked.
prohibited: Given any role change, When roles are changed, Then stranding open work or removing the final admin is prohibited.
boundary: Given the last-admin removal attempt, When committed, Then it is refused.
failure: Given concurrent shared-role or new-assignment edits, When racing, Then required authority is never silently removed.
requirements.verificationMethod: Real-DB access-guard and direct denial tests

requirements.title: Controlled reference data
requirements.description: Stable master IDs and historical snapshots; fixed lifecycle; reference-only outreach/stores.
requirements.securityPrivacy: Apply current grants/scope, minimise sensitive data and preserve trustworthy history.
acceptanceCriteria: positive: Given stable master IDs and historical snapshots, When referenced by approvals or reporting, Then edits never break the references.
negative: Given an archived hierarchy or product, When selected for new work, Then it is unavailable.
prohibited: Given status mutations, When a master record is mutated, Then changing reference semantics in place is prohibited.
boundary: Given a referenced delete racing a new reference, When both commit, Then the delete is rejected.
failure: Given an incompatible reference change, When detected, Then dependent records keep their historical snapshot.

requirements.title: Identity/recovery truth
requirements.description: Authenticated staff provider and actual verification/delivery states replace simulated role/reset.
requirements.securityPrivacy: Apply current grants/scope, minimise sensitive data and preserve trustworthy history.
acceptanceCriteria: positive: Given the chosen identity provider, When staff authenticate, Then actual verification and delivery states are used.
negative: Given an altered or revoked token, When presented, Then access is denied and identity is re-checked per request.
prohibited: Given a verified state, When it is presented as evidence, Then presenting it as proof-of-send is prohibited.
boundary: Given an expired or reused recovery token, When presented, Then it is refused.
failure: Given an identity-provider failure or configuration error, When login is attempted, Then it fails closed and the state is observable.

requirements.title: Evidence and privacy
requirements.description: Quarantine/type/size/checksum/scan and current authorised download protect files/PII.
requirements.securityPrivacy: Apply current grants/scope, minimise sensitive data and preserve trustworthy history.
acceptanceCriteria: positive: Given an uploaded file, When stored, Then quarantine, type, size, checksum and scan state are recorded and download requires current authorisation.
negative: Given hidden data, When any projection runs, Then it is never returned.
prohibited: Given an unclean or failed-scan file, When it is used or downloaded, Then using it as evidence or downloading it is prohibited.
boundary: Given the exact size or type limit, When one unit over is uploaded, Then it is refused.
failure: Given a scanner outage or corrupted stored file, When accessed, Then it stays quarantined or unreadable and the case is flagged.

requirements.title: Atomic audited commands
requirements.description: Domain/tasks/audit/outbox/idempotency commit together with exact snapshots and no partial failure.
requirements.securityPrivacy: Apply current grants/scope, minimise sensitive data and preserve trustworthy history.
acceptanceCriteria: positive: Given a valid command, When committed, Then domain, tasks, audit, outbox and idempotency commit together with exact snapshots.
negative: Given a denied business mutation, When attempted, Then accepted facts are unchanged.
prohibited: Given any command, When it commits, Then partial or torn multi-record writes are prohibited.
boundary: Given an identical retry with the same idempotency key, When replayed, Then the original effect stands and no second effect occurs.
failure: Given a deadlock or database outage mid-transaction, When recovered, Then rollback leaves no torn state.
requirements.verificationMethod: DB rollback/idempotency and version race tests

requirements.title: Accessible matched UI
requirements.description: Preserve prototype visual language with production selectors, state feedback, keyboard and narrow identity fixes.
requirements.securityPrivacy: Apply current grants/scope, minimise sensitive data and preserve trustworthy history.
acceptanceCriteria: positive: Given the approved screenshots, When the React UI is compared, Then visible structure and hierarchy match.
negative: Given 350px and 390px narrow viewports, When identity is displayed, Then it stays readable.
prohibited: Given the prototype source, When a build or refactor consumes it, Then executing or refactoring it as application code is prohibited.
boundary: Given dialogs, comboboxes, focus, error and draft flows, When exercised by keyboard, Then focus and errors behave accessibly.
failure: Given a missing approved screenshot for a screen, When visual parity is claimed, Then the claim is refused and the gap is recorded.

requirements.title: Recovery and capacity
requirements.description: Agree volume/SLO/retention/RPO/RTO and rehearse DB/file/job restore before live use.
requirements.securityPrivacy: Apply current grants/scope, minimise sensitive data and preserve trustworthy history.
acceptanceCriteria: positive: Given agreed volume, SLO, retention, RPO and RTO, When restore and replay are rehearsed, Then restored balances, files, audit and jobs reconcile.
negative: Given unratified targets, When performance is discussed, Then no commitment is claimed.
prohibited: Given a rehearsal with unrecovered gaps, When the gate is evaluated, Then passing the release gate is prohibited.
boundary: Given the approved load envelope, When tested at its exact limit, Then targets hold; one step over shows degradation, not silent failure.
failure: Given a partial database or object restore, When detected, Then the gap is reported and reconciliation runs before use.

requirements.securityPrivacy: Apply current grants/scope, minimise sensitive data and preserve trustworthy history.
requirements.title: Performance targets
requirements.description: Response-time targets from HLD §9 (p95 normal save/search ≤2s, initial usable view ≤3s, due-work processing ≤60s after transition) are design targets to validate under the D-12 agreed envelope of 200 staff, 50k tickets, 100k attachments and peak 50 case events per hour; they are not customer SLAs.
acceptanceCriteria: positive: Given ratified response-time targets, When measured at p95 under the agreed load, Then save/search and initial-view latency meet the ratified values.
negative: Given measurement above the ratified target, When reviewed, Then the release gate fails.
prohibited: Given unratified figures, When they are presented, Then presenting them as committed SLAs is prohibited.
boundary: Given exactly the ratified p95 threshold, When measured, Then it counts as met; one millisecond over fails.
failure: Given measurement-infrastructure failure during a load test, When the run completes, Then the result is invalid, not passing.
requirements.verificationMethod: Load measurement against the HLD §9 p95 targets under the D-12 agreed load envelope

requirements.securityPrivacy: Apply current grants/scope, minimise sensitive data and preserve trustworthy history.
requirements.title: Capacity envelope
requirements.description: The D-12 agreed envelope is 200 staff, 50k tickets, 100k attachments (~50GB) and a peak of 50 case events per hour; capacity is sized against this envelope and forecast growth beyond it triggers capacity work before user impact.
requirements.businessJustification: Size the platform against an agreed envelope, not a guess.
acceptanceCriteria: positive: Given agreed users, records, attachments and peaks, When the system is sized, Then each dimension has a recorded envelope.
negative: Given growth beyond the envelope, When forecast, Then capacity work is triggered before user impact.
prohibited: Given no ratified envelope, When capacity is claimed, Then claiming proven capacity is prohibited.
boundary: Given exactly the agreed peak, When sustained, Then behaviour stays within the ratified availability and performance targets.
failure: Given storage, memory or connection exhaustion inside the envelope, When it occurs, Then it is treated as a defect against the capacity record.
requirements.verificationMethod: Capacity model and headroom test against the agreed D-12 envelope

requirements.securityPrivacy: Apply current grants/scope, minimise sensitive data and preserve trustworthy history.
requirements.title: Availability target
requirements.description: D-12 sets 99.5% monthly uptime measured excluding the first Sunday 02:00–04:00 UTC maintenance window; HLD §9 records Multi-AZ and redundancy as subject to this target. Outages crossing the window boundary are attributed per the agreed convention.
requirements.businessJustification: Make availability an explicit ratified commitment, not an assumption.
acceptanceCriteria: positive: Given a ratified uptime target, When measured over the agreed window, Then actual availability meets it or an incident is recorded.
negative: Given unratified uptime, When communicated, Then it is described as a proposal, not a commitment.
prohibited: Given any measurement window, When availability is reported, Then silently excluding outages from it is prohibited.
boundary: Given the exact measurement-window boundary, When an outage crosses it, Then it is attributed per the agreed convention.
failure: Given a dependency outage, When it reduces availability, Then the impact is measured and reported.
requirements.verificationMethod: Availability measurement over the monthly window with the agreed first-Sunday 02:00–04:00 UTC exclusion

requirements.securityPrivacy: Apply current grants/scope, minimise sensitive data and preserve trustworthy history.
requirements.title: Recovery objectives
requirements.description: D-12 sets RPO 15min and RTO 4h; D-11 sets case-evidence retention of 7 years and audit-log retention of 2 years append-only. Rehearsal obligations exist (REQ-028); recovery capability is only claimed when a timed restore rehearsal meets these objectives.
requirements.businessJustification: Recovery claims need ratified objectives and measured rehearsals.
acceptanceCriteria: positive: Given ratified RPO/RTO and retention, When a restore is rehearsed, Then measured values meet them.
negative: Given a rehearsal miss, When measured, Then the gate fails until a successful re-rehearsal.
prohibited: Given unratified objectives, When recovery is claimed, Then claiming recovery capability is prohibited.
boundary: Given data at the exact RPO edge, When restored, Then the loss window equals the ratified tolerance, no more.
failure: Given a partial restore, When detected, Then the affected scope is quarantined and reconciled before use.
requirements.verificationMethod: Timed restore rehearsal against the agreed RPO 15min / RTO 4h

requirements.securityPrivacy: Apply current grants/scope, minimise sensitive data and preserve trustworthy history.
requirements.title: Security posture baseline
requirements.description: D-03 records Google Workspace OIDC SSO for all staff with no local passwords, mandatory MFA for Super/Finance/privileged roles and optional for ordinary CS, single-use 24h emailed invitations, admin-assisted recovery with recorded identity evidence, 30min idle / 12h absolute sessions revoked on password or role change or admin action, and mail via Google Workspace SMTP; D-11 records masking of customer email, phone and attachment values in exports by default. HLD §8 MFA for privileged and finance roles is an approved control.
requirements.businessJustification: Security controls must be ratified, not inferred from a proposal.
acceptanceCriteria: positive: Given a ratified identity, MFA, session and privacy baseline, When staff authenticate, Then the ratified controls apply.
negative: Given a gap against the ratified baseline, When reviewed, Then it blocks release.
prohibited: Given unresolved identity or privacy decisions, When the affected behaviour is launched, Then launching the affected behaviour is prohibited.
boundary: Given privileged and finance roles versus ordinary roles, When the MFA policy applies, Then privileged/finance users are covered per the ratified proposal.
failure: Given a compromised dependency or CI action or a leaked secret, When detected, Then revocation, containment and review follow the security policy.
requirements.verificationMethod: Control review against the recorded identity and privacy baseline (D-03, D-11)

requirements.securityPrivacy: Apply current grants/scope, minimise sensitive data and preserve trustworthy history.
requirements.title: Monthly budget ceiling
requirements.description: D-12 records a USD 500/month ceiling with alerts at 80%, AWS as the deployment provider and eu-west-1 (Ireland) with EU data residency; spend is tracked against the recorded ceiling.
requirements.businessJustification: Avoid unbounded or invented infrastructure spend.
acceptanceCriteria: positive: Given a ratified monthly budget, When spend is tracked, Then actuals are compared against it.
negative: Given a forecast overrun, When detected, Then it is raised before the month closes.
prohibited: Given no ratified budget, When infrastructure is provisioned, Then provisioning paid infrastructure is prohibited.
boundary: Given spend at exactly the ratified ceiling, When reached, Then new capacity requires approval.
failure: Given a cost anomaly, When observed, Then it is investigated as an operational event.
requirements.verificationMethod: Spend tracking against the agreed USD 500/month ceiling
